pages_convention: XML section and paragraph locators (jats_text) for the abstract and captions. The XML text has no body text, so body steps use printed journal pages (276–295) from the PDF. Figure-content steps cite the caption label and the printed page, e.g. 'Fig. 10 (p. 291)'.

entry.evidence: However, the tectonic-magmatic setting remains problematic, which hinders understanding the factors that control the gold endowment in the region.

sequences.source_document: Wang et al. 2022 published PDF with XML abstract and captions

steps.action: The authors pose the unsolved question of the tectonic setting of Early Cretaceous low-sulfidation epithermal gold deposits in NE China.
steps.quote: the tectonic setting of the epithermal gold deposits remains controversial

steps.action: They take from the literature two rival tectonic models: Mongol–Okhotsk post-collision extension, or back-arc extension from Paleo-Pacific slab rollback.
steps.quote: post-collision extension of Okhotsk subduction or back-arc extension of Paleo-Pacific slab rollback

steps.action: They choose the Wulaga deposit as a case study, combining geochronological and geochemical data on the ore-related porphyry to constrain petrogenesis and setting.
steps.quote: we take the Wulaga gold deposit as a case study, integrating geochronological and geochemical data

steps.action: They describe the deposit geology (fault-controlled apophyses, crypto-explosive breccia, orebodies) and sample granodiorite porphyry from drill core on exploration line 102.
steps.quote: Geological cross-section of No.102 exploration line of the Wulaga gold deposit.

steps.action: They date 18 zircon rims from sample TJG-1 by LA–ICP–MS, giving a weighted-mean 206Pb/238U crystallization age of 107.7 ± 1.3 Ma.
steps.quote: which is interpreted as the crystallization age of the pluton

steps.action: They measure whole-rock major and trace elements of six new samples by XRF and ICP–MS and tabulate them with published PTG data.
steps.quote: all samples display coherent multi-element variation patterns

steps.action: They check the new bulk-rock data against the earlier analyses of other samples (Wang et al., 2012) and report them comparable.
steps.quote: acquired from our studies are comparable to previous analysis

steps.action: They measure Sr–Nd isotopes by TIMS and in-situ zircon Hf isotopes by LA–MC–ICP–MS on sample WLG-W-1.
steps.quote: The εHf(t) values vary from 6.0 to 8.1.

steps.action: They reuse whole-rock Pb isotope data from their own earlier studies.
steps.quote: The existing whole-rock Pb isotopic results are listed in Table 4 (Wang et al., 2012, 2016).

steps.action: They control the isotope measurements with reference materials: zircon standards bracket the U–Pb runs, and the GJ Hf ratios match reported values (Methods).
steps.quote: agree with the reported values

steps.action: They set the new Southwest-apophysis age beside earlier ages of the North and Southeast apophyses and find that all three agree.
steps.quote: The excellent agreement of the formation ages for the three apophyses indicates that they are formed in the same magmatic event.

steps.action: They compare the porphyry U–Pb ages with the earlier pyrite Rb–Sr ore age (113.8 ± 4.4 Ma) and infer that the mineralization is related to the porphyry.
steps.quote: The close temporal and spatial association suggests that the Wulaga gold mineralization is related to the granodiorite porphyry.

steps.action: They compile published ages from the Dong'an and Sandaowanzi deposits and infer a continuum of Early Cretaceous intrusion-related epithermal mineralization.
steps.quote: these ages suggest a continuum of intrusion-related epithermal gold mineralization

steps.action: Using discrimination diagrams and mineralogy, they classify the porphyry as I-type and reject S-type (no aluminous minerals) and A-type.
steps.quote: suggests that these granites are not S-type granites

steps.action: They state two literature routes to I-type granite: partial melting of juvenile lower crust, or mixing of mantle and ancient-crust melts.
steps.quote: I-type granite can be produced by partial melting of intermediate-mafic metamorphic-volcanic rocks in the juvenile lower crust

steps.action: They compare trace-element ratios, Mg#, Sr–Nd, Pb and Hf isotopes with crust and mantle reservoir values and fields.
steps.quote: plotted between the ancient lower crust and depleted mantle lines in the lead isotope diagrams

steps.action: They keep the source claim: the porphyry derives mainly from partial melting of Neoproterozoic juvenile lower crust.
steps.quote: porphyry predominantly originated from the partial melting of the juvenile lower crust

steps.action: They estimate melting conditions from Zr content and Ti-in-zircon thermometry (about 700 °C), Sr/Y and REE (garnet-stable depth), Ba/La (hydrous fluids) and zircon-based fO2 (high).
steps.quote: formed at depth within the stability field of garnet

steps.action: They review published regional evidence for Paleo-Pacific back-arc extension and for Mongol–Okhotsk closure at about 130 Ma.
steps.quote: the closure of the Mongol–Okhotsk oceanic plate occurred at ~130 Ma

steps.action: They plot the porphyry on tectonic discrimination and adakite diagrams; it falls in the volcanic-arc and adakite fields.
steps.quote: mainly plotted in subduction-related volcanic arc granite

steps.action: They keep a combined setting: an interaction between post-orogenic Mongol–Okhotsk extension and Paleo-Pacific back-arc extension, rather than either rival alone.
steps.quote: formed in the extensional setting triggered by mutual interaction between post-orogenic lithospheric extension

steps.action: They refine this into a tectono-magmatic and ore-forming model: fault reactivation, magma ascent, then fluids mixing with meteoric water in the breccia zone.
steps.quote: ascended along Wulaga deep fault and partly extruded on the surface

tree.answer: Partly: three coeval deposits (Wulaga, Dong'an, Sandaowanzi) from published ages
Limited: agreement with earlier samples and ages, multiple isotope systems
Combined two-regime extensional setting kept as best explanation

end.claim: The Early Cretaceous low-sulfidation epithermal gold deposits of the Xing–Meng Orogenic Belt formed in an extensional setting created by interaction between post-orogenic extension after Mongol–Okhotsk closure and back-arc extension from Paleo-Pacific rollback.

decisive_move.sentence: The setting claim rests on comparing the porphyry's trace-element and isotopic signatures with discrimination diagrams (volcanic-arc and adakite fields), read together with cited regional evidence for both regimes.

gates.evidence: The two rival models are named in the Introduction (p. 277), but sampling and analysis were general geochemistry, not chosen to separate them. The discrimination diagrams could have placed the samples elsewhere (e.g. WPG or S-type), so the I-type and arc claims faced a test. The final 'mutual interaction' claim, however, accommodates both rivals, and no prediction separating them is stated. Nothing was fixed before the data.

imports.item: Laser-ablation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (LA–ICP–MS) for zircon U–Pb and trace elements
Thermal ionization mass spectrometry (Finnigan MAT-262) for Sr–Nd isotopes
Multi-collector ICP–MS (Neptune) with 193 nm laser ablation for zircon Hf isotopes
X-ray fluorescence spectrometry (PW2404) for major elements

limits:
No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded.

Inconsistencies in the text:
- Hf analyses are said to be on 'the exact spots where the U–Pb dating was performed' but are on sample WLG-W-1 (Southeast apophysis; Fig. 1c), while U–Pb is on TJG-1 (Southwest apophysis). The Hf initial ratios use ages from Wang et al. (2012) (pp. 281, 285).
- The Na2O range quoted in the Discussion (2.67–3.33 wt%, p. 287) does not match Table 2 (3.29–4.50 wt%).
- The Pb isotope ranges in §5.3 and §6.2 differ.
- High Mg# (53–64) is read as mantle involvement, yet the kept source is juvenile lower crust. The magma-mixing rival is not explicitly excluded (inference).

Tectonic test (inference): no prediction separating the two tectonic rivals is computed. The same diagrams (VAG, adakite) are read as supporting both, so the combined-setting claim is not exposed to failure. The regional extension to all XMOB deposits rests on cited ages from Dong'an and Sandaowanzi.

Provenance: Pb isotopes and the pyrite Rb–Sr age are the authors' earlier work (inherited). The temperature and fO2 estimates are reported without stated uncertainties.

Sub-claims and their statuses:
- Emplacement age 107.7 ± 1.3 Ma: estimate_with_resolution.
- Porphyry–mineralization coevality: best_explanation.
- Juvenile lower-crust source: best_explanation.
- Melting conditions (about 700 °C, water-rich, high fO2, garnet-stable): estimate_with_resolution, uncertainties unstated.

Anomalous spot: zircon spot TJG-1-6 has anomalous Ti (4846 ppm) and no T or fO2 reported; this is not discussed.

disagreements.quote: With recent advances in chemical procedures and mass spectrometer techniques, more precise isotopic geochronology data

disagreements.support: Discrimination diagrams (volcanic-arc and adakite affinity) and cited regional geology are read as consistent with both regimes acting together.
disagreements.quote: not only related to the subduction of the PaleoPacific Ocean Plate, but also consistent with the closure of the Mongol-Okhotsk Ocean

alternatives_considered.reason: Na2O vs K2O plot in I-type field; absence of aluminous minerals (muscovite, tourmaline, garnet); biotite-bearing assemblage

alternatives_considered.chosen: Partial melting of juvenile (Neoproterozoic) mafic lower crust
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Magmatic mixing of mantle- and ancient crust-derived melts
alternatives_considered.reason: Sr–Nd–Pb–Hf isotopes and young model ages together with major and trace element evidence

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Zircon saturation thermometry (Watson and Harrison, 1983), mentioned but not computed

alternatives_considered.chosen: Combined setting: Mongol–Okhotsk post-orogenic extension interacting with Paleo-Pacific back-arc extension
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Paleo-Pacific subduction/rollback alone; Mongol–Okhotsk closure alone
alternatives_considered.reason: Arc and adakite geochemical affinity plus regional evidence for both regimes
